subject: math
greeting: Good evening — let's explore one of the most beautiful equations in mathematics.
needed_formulas: z = \cos(\theta) + i\sin(\theta) \text{ on the unit circle}
assumptions: You know what complex numbers are (a + bi).
You are comfortable with sine and cosine on the unit circle.
Radians measure angle around the origin.
Mobjects_needed: Circle radius=1 for the unit circle
Line from origin to the dot
Axes for real and imaginary components
learning_objectives: Understand that e^{ix} traces the unit circle as x varies.
See cos(x) and sin(x) as the real and imaginary parts of e^{ix}.
Connect rotation in the complex plane to exponential form.

storyboard_beats.title: Opener
storyboard_beats.narration: Have you ever wondered how exponentials and circles are secretly the same idea? Euler's formula reveals that connection.
storyboard_beats.visual: Title 'Euler's Formula' and subtitle with the main equation centered on a flat 2D board.

storyboard_beats.title: The formula
storyboard_beats.narration: Here is the identity: e to the i x equals cosine x plus i sine x.
storyboard_beats.visual: Write MathTex e^{ix} = \cos(x) + i\sin(x); hold on screen while naming each term.

storyboard_beats.title: Complex plane setup
storyboard_beats.narration: Picture the complex plane: horizontal real axis, vertical imaginary axis.
storyboard_beats.visual: Fade in Axes; label Real and Imaginary; keep margins inside frame.

storyboard_beats.title: Unit circle
storyboard_beats.narration: Every point on the unit circle can be written as cosine theta plus i sine theta.

storyboard_beats.title: Rotating vector
storyboard_beats.narration: As theta sweeps from zero to two pi, the tip of this vector traces the circle.
storyboard_beats.visual: Arrow from origin to Dot; animate theta with ValueTracker or parametric motion.

storyboard_beats.title: Real and imaginary parts
storyboard_beats.narration: The horizontal projection is cosine theta; the vertical projection is sine theta.
storyboard_beats.visual: Show dashed projections to axes; label cos(theta) and sin(theta).

storyboard_beats.title: Exponential form
storyboard_beats.narration: That rotating point is exactly e to the i theta — exponential form meets geometry.
storyboard_beats.visual: Transform or ReplacementTransform linking e^{i\theta} label to the moving dot.

storyboard_beats.title: Special case
storyboard_beats.narration: At pi radians, e to the i pi equals negative one — the famous Euler identity.
storyboard_beats.visual: Pause at theta=pi; flash e^{i\pi}+1=0 briefly.

storyboard_beats.title: Takeaways
storyboard_beats.narration: You just saw how rotation, trig, and exponentials are one story on the unit circle.
storyboard_beats.visual: Two-column takeaway list inside SurroundingRectangle; no overflow past frame edges.

voiceover_notes: Use VoiceoverScene with short beats; every visual change needs a spoken line. Prefer present tense, second person.
